request.title: Peach Bounce 0.3 — Orbital Fruit Rescue
request.prompt:
PEACH BOUNCE 0.3 — SUBSTANTIAL GAMEPLAY REDESIGN OF GRAVITY SLING, not a cosmetic patch. Update only docs/games/studio-original-001/ and preserve the stable public game URL. The supplied screenshot of 0.2 shows wasted height and an old catch-and-relaunch mechanic; those are the primary problems.

VISION: Portrait-first, one-finger, physics-based puzzle/space survival game. Use tall Samsung/Android screens deliberately: TOP FIELD is where ordered fruit enters, moves, and is harvested; BOTTOM SHIP ZONE is where the player drags the ship horizontally and governs the gravity/slingshot. Treat ship, probe, cargo, resources, orbital arc and danger as visually legible separate concepts. Game field should dominate the viewport, without a tall header, bottom buttons or prose forcing a page scroll. Portrait 360x800, 390x844 and 412x915 must be comfortable, with safe-area insets and immediate touch response. Desktop A/D/arrow control and accessible buttons remain.

REPLACE 0.2 CORE MECHANIC:
- Ship launches a probe upward (initial speed/tangent tuned for reliable near-miss orbit) as soon as play begins, and automatically launches replacements when appropriate.
- Each active probe moves under continuous time-step simulated ship gravity and momentum, with coherent, observable curved paths. The player repositions the ship in the lower zone to redirect/assist the moving probe; it swings AROUND the ship and accelerates outward again, not teleported or magically caught/relaunched at a crossing. Make gravity softened, numerically stable, and give the probe an angular/tangential motion or carefully designed assist so viable looping returns are achievable. Visualize trajectory and a distinct ring: ship collision radius INSIDE, safe cargo deposit radius OUTSIDE; deposit requires a genuine approach/near pass, not guaranteed each frame. No existing code's catch crossing that flips vy.
- The returning probe must NOT land on or enter the ship. If probe collides with ship's solid collision radius, BOTH hull -1 AND probe stock -1, with clean temporary damage feedback and new probe deployment if supply remains.
- If probe leaves the screen/arena, becomes too distant for a meaningful orbit, or simulation detects a genuinely lost flight, probe stock -1 and a fresh probe deploys if available. Escapes must not damage hull. Distinguish crash versus escape in HUD/messages. Prevent duplicate loss on same flight and impossible infinite orbit/stuck probe.
- Fruit is spawned/arrives in the upper zone in clearly indicated numerical order (1,2,3...), not near the ship at start. The probe physically passes THROUGH fruit, harvesting it rather than bouncing off it or becoming permanently destroyed. Segment/swept collision for fast probes. Correct numbered targets count as carried cargo; preserve uncollected/wrong-order logic and make it visually obvious what to hit next. An incorrect hit must not secretly clear the fruit or add currency.
- Cargo travels visibly with the probe and is BANKED only upon a close SAFE orbital pass around the ship (near, but outside the solid impact radius). Banking is separate from damage and from mere fruit contact. Lost probe loses unbanked cargo; the corresponding targets must reappear/requeue so no ordered-wave soft lock or duplication exploit.
- Each banked fruit = one repair/build unit. Allocate each unit to +1 HULL while hull is below MAX HULL; only once hull is full, allocate +1 spare PROBE (subject to a visible reasonable capacity). This is a deterministic priority rule, not score-only. When multiple fruit arrive, apply units one by one in that order. Show banking, hull repair, probe construction clearly.
- Survival/puzzle challenge: expendable probes, damaging ship collisions, moving ordered fruit, changing gravity from ship movement, resource management. Avoid making all returns automatic or impossible; skillful positioning matters. Producer can decide coherent waves/progression/end state, but fruit must continue to be available for sustainable survival and earned resources, not a trivial static three-wave demo.
- 0.3 visible title/version throughout; no Cataclysm, Neon Salvage, workflow, dashboard or other game changes. Keep 0.2 source recoverable through Git history. No external dependencies/services.

REQUIRED TESTS AND EVIDENCE: deterministic fixed-step simulation or accessible test seam for representative near-miss bank, direct collision (-1 hull and -1 probe), offscreen escape (-1 probe only), ordered fruit pickup, correct cargo accounting/priority (hull repair first, then probe), loss of cargo + target recovery, and pause/resume/reset. Independently play with real pointer/keyboard events (not only state injection) on 360x800, 390x844, 412x915 and desktop. Confirm that start actually advances, the probe visibly curves, ship drag works, controls never hide beneath browser UI, canvas doesn't stretch physics/collision positions, and game has a survivable reproducible play path. If acceptance fails, do not ship a cosmetic fallback. Council should plan physics and game economy jointly; QA should challenge cases where near pass is interpreted as collision and where resources duplicate.

Feedback reference: GitHub issue https://github.com/BoRHeX/kbc-rpg-prototype/issues/44.
acceptance: Visible title/version Peach Bounce 0.3; same /games/studio-original-001/ URL, distinct stamped build; other games and studio unchanged.
Phone portrait 360x800, 390x844 and 412x915: top fruit playfield, bottom drag ship area, responsive canvas/HUD and all controls within viewport without page scroll or overlap.
Probe launches and follows curved gravity-based continuous motion; near-pass slingshots outward without teleport, vy sign-flip catch or landing inside the ship.
Probe-ship collision removes exactly 1 hull and 1 probe; escape/excess-radius loss removes exactly 1 probe and no hull; each lost probe replaced once when stock available.
Correct numbered fruit hit by swept probe collision becomes visibly carried cargo; wrong-order fruit remains; hitting fruit does not automatically credit hull/probes.
Safe deposit annulus banks cargo without impact; inner solid radius causes damage, not reward; no unlimited repeat deposits from lingering in ring.
Each banked fruit repairs hull by +1 until max, then creates +1 probe while respecting capacity; resource HUD reflects exact changes, loss and full-resource behavior.
Crash/escape discards unbanked fruit; ordered fruit recovers/requeues with no stuck wave, duplicate profit or impossible objective.
Survival loop includes continuing fruit/progression and clear defeat/replay, with actual player-controlled trajectory influence and skill-dependent success.
Pause/resume/restart, touch drag, A/D/arrow keys, and Play controls function after loss or completion; no runaway simulation, frame-rate-dependent physics or canvas collision scaling errors.
Independent automated gameplay trajectories and mobile browser input tests document results; publish only if QA approves and live bytes match accepted build.

designer.claim: Implement a fruit-wave progression and perspective visualization subsystem for the gravity sling game upgrade 0.3, including clear top playfield for ordered fruit waves with distinct numbered fruit, distinct fruit shapes/colors, and a legible, tall portrait layout with ship confined to bottom drag zone and visible contextual instructions.
designer.rationale: The requested gameplay redesign 0.3 emphasizes a portrait-first layout leveraging tall phone aspect ratios with a distinct separation of top fruit zone and bottom ship control zone. Ordered fruit waves must be visually presented in a clear vertical perspective with fruit growing as they approach the ship, each fruit visually distinct and numbered for intuitive targeting order. Instructions on the gameplay flow must remain legible without crowding or scrolling. Existing control scheme and core mechanics are preserved but extended by improved wave and perspective visualization to communicate game state and challenge effectively on mobile.
objections: Implementation must ensure the new fruit wave color and shape variety does not impair collision detection or accessibility.
Additional fruit shapes should be programmatically defined to avoid external assets, increasing code complexity.
Careful scaling and aspect ratio management needed to avoid UI overlap or loss of interactive area on different phones.
High fruit count or large shapes might impact performance on low-end devices; optimization is needed.

feature.name: Fruit Wave Progression and Perspective Visual Subsystem
feature.player_experience: Players experience a visually rich, clearly readable fruit playfield at the top half of the screen where fruits appear in distinct numbered order, with unique shapes and colors for each fruit type. The ship resides in the bottom zone, controlled horizontally by touch or keyboard. The gameplay instructions remain concise and always visible below the fruit zone but above controls. Fruit are drawn in a vertical tilted perspective with dynamic scaling to convey depth, helping players anticipate timing and approach for harvesting in correct order.

code_changes.pseudo_code: Refactor to render fruit in top 'fruit orbit' zone with enhanced vertical depth scaling (larger near bottom, smaller near top). Draw numbered fruit with unique shapes: peach (lobed shape), pear (round shoulder shape), plum (ellipse). Emphasize NEXT target fruit with larger highlight ring. Maintain fruit layering by depth for natural overlap. Add atmospheric shading with horizon gradient. Remove previous fixed circular fruits; define fruit shape drawing directly in canvas 2D instructions.

Replace detailed multi-line paragraph describing controls and catch mechanics with concise instruction: 'Slide ship below in bottom zone to slingshot probe. Harvest fruit in ascending order at top field.' Update title version span id='game-version' to '0.3'.

Adjust main and canvas styles to maximize vertical space. Define top fruit zone to use about 60% height and bottom ship control zone about 40%. Use safe-area insets for padding. Adjust font sizes and line heights in header and stats for clarity and balance with tall portrait modes. Ensure no layout overflow or scrolling on 360x800, 390x844, 412x915 viewport sizes.

tests: Verify fruits appear at top zone and scale progressively larger near bottom zone visually.
Test NEXT target fruit is distinctively highlighted with a glowing ring and larger size.
Validate fruit numbering matches ascending order and correct fruit reacts to collision.
Check ship controls restrict movement to bottom zone only and respond to horizontal drag.
Confirm instructions text is visible, concise, and stable without causing scroll.
Test stable frame rates and rendering on 360x800, 390x844, and 412x915 portrait emulations.

required_evidence: Gameplay screen captures showing tall portrait layout with distinct top fruit field and bottom ship drag zone on phones 360x800, 390x844, 412x915.
Automated test logs verifying correct fruit ordering, shape distinction, and layering in drawing sequence.
Recorded test session confirming responsive horizontal ship drag only in bottom zone and correct probe trajectories through fruit waves.
Accessibility inspection report verifying text readibility and no overlap or scroll in instructions and HUD.
Performance benchmarks on emulated low-end mobile devices showing smooth rendering and frame rates.
Code static analysis reports confirming no regression to input or physics simulation functions.

researcher.claim: Implement a full orbital probe flight and cargo banking subsystem with gravity sling mechanics, replacing the old catch-and-relaunch crossing with continuous curved orbits and distinct collision zones.
researcher.rationale: The request demands a redesign for version 0.3 focusing on continuous time-step gravitational physics simulating coherent curved probe trajectories influenced by ship position and velocity, with a near-miss stable orbit allowing the probe to swing around the ship without teleportation or velocity sign-flips. The probe must not enter the ship; instead, close passes outside a solid collision radius form a safe cargo deposit zone to bank collected fruit. Probe-ship collisions cause hull and probe loss with feedback and immediate replacement if available. Probe escapes offscreen lose a probe without hull damage. Fruit appear in order in the top zone and are physically passed through by the probe to pick up cargo, which must be separately banked at deposit. Lost probes discard unbanked cargo and requeue the associated fruit to preserve game continuation without wave lock. Banked fruit recovers hull first then builds probes deterministically. This preserves ship horizontal dragging controls and accessible layout, and retains pause/restart and diagnostic API as required. The proposal integrates orbit visualization and collision radius logic in game.js while adjusting UI elements if needed to fit the portrait layout without overlay or scroll.
objections: Implementation risk of stable continuous near-miss orbits without numerical instability or forced velocity flips is high and requires careful physics tuning.
Additional state for cargo onboard probe and banking logic will increase complexity, potentially impacting performance on low-end mobile devices.
Visual complexity of separate cargo tracking and distinct ring zones may affect clarity if not carefully designed, risking player confusion.
New mechanics demand comprehensive testing for all edge cases: collisions, cargo loss, wave progression, and recovery of lost fruit; bugs could disrupt game flow or cause soft locks.
Integration with existing pause/resume and player input handling must be seamless to prevent input lag or inconsistent state.
No changes are proposed for UI text, but the added HUD elements for cargo and banking resource counts require design considerations for small viewport spaces.

feature.name: Orbital Probe Flight and Cargo Banking Subsystem
feature.player_experience: Players control the ship horizontally in the bottom zone, launching probes that arc in realistic gravitational orbits around the ship with momentum and softened gravity. Probes collect fruit in order by passing through them. Rather than instant catch-and-relaunch, players skillfully maneuver the ship to create near-miss orbits that deposit cargo safely in a distinct ring outside the ship collision radius, banking resources to repair hull or build probes. Probe collisions damage the ship and use up probes; escapes lose probes only. Players feel deep engagement from balancing probe preservation, mid-air maneuvering, and cargo banking to survive progressively challenging fruit waves.

code_changes.pseudo_code: Refactor gravitySlingSubsystem to apply softened inverse-square gravitational acceleration with finite force at ship center and apply angular/tangential velocity assist for stable orbits. Compute probe movement continuously via fixed timestep integration without velocity sign flips. Track probe position and velocity, updating path accordingly.

Implement probeShipCollision check: if probe position enters ship collision radius, decrement hull and probes, trigger damage feedback, and drop probe. Implement probeEscape check: if probe position leaves arena bounds or orbit criteria fail, decrement probe stock only and redeploy probe if available. Implement cargo banking logic: when probe passes safely within deposit annulus outside collision radius, bank cargo items in FIFO order; apply hull repair first then probe construction, update HUD accordingly.

In updateFruit or during gravitySlingSubsystem, perform swept segment collision between probe and ordered active fruit. On correct hit, attach fruit cargo to probe without removing fruit immediately from wave progression. On wrong-order hit, flash indication without progress.

Integrate calls to new probeCollisionAndBanking and fruitPickupDetection functions. Maintain fixed timestep and ship horizontal movement input unchanged. Emit events for probe lost, hull damaged, cargo banked, with relevant messaging.

Add orbital path visualization with tessellated curved probe trail showing trajectory and cargo carried. Draw distinct inner ship collision radius and concentric safe cargo deposit annulus with subtle differences in stroke style. Display cargo icon/badge on probe.

tests: Deterministic fixed-step simulation test of probe orbit showing near-miss banking pass without velocity sign-flip.
Direct ship collision test verifies exactly 1 hull and 1 probe reduction, damage feedback, and probe redeploy if stock remains.
Offscreen probe escape test removes exactly 1 probe without hull damage and spawns replacement if probes available.
Ordered fruit pickup test confirms only correct numbered fruit are collected as cargo; hitting wrong order triggers visual feedback only.
Cargo banking test verifies unbanked cargo is banked one unit at a time upon safe orbit pass, repairing hull first then adding probes with capacity limits.
Lost probe cargo recovery test confirms unbanked cargo lost upon probe loss; lost fruit is respawned/requeued in correct order without duplication or soft lock.

required_evidence: Deterministic simulation traces of probe orbital trajectories confirming continuous gravity and tangential assist produce stable looping returns and banking passes.
Recorded test sequences demonstrating correct hull and probe adjustments on direct collisions and escapes.
Evidence of correct ordered fruit pickup and cargo carriage, separate from banking, with visual feedback for both correct hits and wrong-order hits.
UI state updates showing exact hull and probe counts before and after collisions, escapes, and banking events.
Pause and resume maintain physics state and cargo banking logic consistency with no loss or duplication.
Mobile viewport screenshots or videos demonstrating that top fruit field and bottom ship drag zones remain visible and accessible without scroll or obscuration, including cargo banking HUD elements.

engineer.claim: Introduce a precise ship-probe collision and safe cargo deposit subsystem with survivable difficulty scaling integrated into the existing gravity sling gameplay, replacing the legacy catch-and-relaunch mechanic.
engineer.rationale: The current gameplay uses an unrealistic catch/relaunch flip at a crossing threshold allowing the probe to land inside the ship, which is rejected by the player feedback. Implementing a continuous time-step physics-based probe orbit with numerical softening to enable stable curved trajectories around the ship lets the probe physically swing around and accelerate outward again, eliminating teleportation and sign-flipping artifacts. Adding distinct collision radii for the ship's solid hull and a surrounding safe cargo deposit annulus enforces genuine near-passes for banking cargo. Probe collisions with the ship reduce hull and probe counts by exactly one each with proper damage feedback and trigger auto deployment if probes remain. Probe escapes offscreen or too distant consume one probe without hull damage. Cargo collected in order travels visibly with the probe and is banked only upon a safe near pass outside the collision radius, preserving ordered waves and required priority resource allocation (repair hull up to max, then add probes respecting capacity). This system fosters skillful play, resource management, and clear feedback, supporting sustainable survival without trivially automatic returns or unavoidable losses while respecting existing one-axis controls and mobile layouts.
objections: Implementing precise segment/swept collisions and stable soft gravity loops can risk numerical instability or infinite orbit states if not carefully tuned.
Distinguishing probe loss by crash versus escape requires robust logic to prevent duplicate loss accounting and soft-locks on target waves during cargo loss and requeueing.
The visual and accessibility demands for feedback on cargo banking, hull damage, and probe resources may complicate UI layout on small viewports.
Added complexity could increase CPU use on lower-end mobiles, risking performance regressions.
Prior mechanic removal risks player frustration if new trajectory controls feel less direct or responsive initially.
Ensuring all edge cases of pause/resume/reset and keyboard/touch input consistency introduces integration challenges.

feature.name: Orbital Probe Collision and Cargo Banking Subsystem
feature.player_experience: Players control a horizontally draggable ship at the bottom. Automatically launched probes arc under ship gravity, visibly curving around the ship with a distinct visible tether. Probes physically swing around avoiding collision with the ship's solid hull radius; if a probe collides, it causes precise hull and probe loss with damage feedback. Cargo pickups occur only in correct numeric order, visibly carried by probes, and are banked only when the probe safely passes outside a designated annular zone around the ship. Failed cargo (if probe is lost) respawns to allow retry, preventing soft-locks. Resource HUD updates reflect hull repairs first, then probe stock increases, showing clear survivable difficulty progression. The integration preserves one-axis drag input and mobile controls.

code_changes.pseudo_code: Refactor probe motion to incorporate softened inverse-square gravity centered on ship position; calculate gravitational acceleration vector, including ship's lateral velocity influence; integrate probe velocity and position using fixed timestep; clamp velocity magnitudes; track probe age and handle auto-deployment on probe loss (escape or collision).

After updating probe physics, perform detailed swept segment collision checks between probe trajectory and (a) ordered fruit with numbered priority, to assign cargo correctly without removal on wrong hits; (b) ship collision radius for direct hull and probe damage with temporary invulnerability cooldown; (c) 'safe deposit' annulus for cargo banking when probe passes near but outside hull radius, applying hull first repair then probe increments respecting max limits. Update cargo, hull, and probes state accordingly.

Implement invulnerability timer and collision handling: on probe-ship collision, decrement hull and probes by one, reject additional hull damage during invulnerability, trigger damage message and feedback, and spawn a replacement probe if available. Distinctly separate cargo banking logic.
Maintain ordered wave progression with fruits moving top to bottom; reset fruit on loss of cargo due to probe destruction; ensure no duplication of cleared targets and visibly indicate next fruit.

Define two radii: inner collision radius and outer safe deposit radius of ship; track cargo carried by probes; when probe crosses the safe deposit annulus outward with cargo, bank each fruit one by one: increment hull if below max, else increment probe stock up to max, remove cargo from probe, and reflect changes on HUD.

Visualize probe orbit arcs tethered to ship; render cargo visibly attached to probes; highlight safe deposit zone as annulus around ship; provide damage feedback flashes on hull hits; show numeric HUD updates for hull and probes reflecting real-time changes.

tests: Simulate a near-miss probe orbit looping around the ship, verifying no collision and banking cargo upon safe pass.
Test direct collision between probe and ship, confirm exactly one hull and one probe loss, invulnerability cooldown triggers, and replacement probe deploys.
Force probe escape offscreen, confirm exactly one probe loss with no hull damage, auto-deploy replacement if probes remain.
Confirm fruit pickups only trigger when probe collides with correct next-numbered fruit; hitting wrong order causes visual feedback and no progress.
Validate cargo banking correctly prioritizes hull repair up to max before adding probes, with HUD reflecting exact state.
Test loss of probe while carrying cargo causes cargo to be lost and associated fruit to requeue for reattempt, with no stuck waves or duplication exploits.

required_evidence: Deterministic fixed-step simulation logs showing stable probe orbits with continuous gravity and tangential momentum preserving curvature.
Automated test logs recording discrete probe-ship collision events decrementing hull and probes exactly once per collision.
Recorded runs demonstrating safe cargo deposit annulus functionality distinctly separate from collision radius with corresponding HUD resource increments.
Visual evidence screenshots/videos of probe-cargo linkage, cargo banking feedback, hull damage flash, and probe escape handling on mobile portrait resolutions 360x800, 390x844, 412x915.
Independent mobile browser input automated tests validating pointer and keyboard horizontal control responsiveness and pause/resume/restart functionality preserving precise gameplay state.
Code static analysis confirming fixed time-step physics integration correctness, swept collision checks, resource priority management, stable state transitions on damage, escape, and banking events.

critic.claim: The combined gravity sling gameplay redesign integrates three complementary subsystems—designer's visual fruit progression, researcher's orbital probe and cargo banking mechanics, and engineer's collision and resource update handling—forming a complex but coherent player experience.
critic.rationale: The proposals collectively redefine gameplay zones, probe physics, and feedback loops to deliver a polished mobile game mechanic where players horizontally control a ship and launch probes in gravity-affected orbits to collect fruit in order and manage resources. Visual, physics, collision, and UI aspects align around the core requirement of one-axis control and ordered fruit harvesting with cargo banking under gravity sling mechanics.
objections: Potential symbol conflicts arise as both researcher and engineer modify 'gravitySlingSubsystem' and 'step' functions, risking overwrites or inconsistent physics and collision behavior if not carefully merged.

The delayed fruit removal (researcher's approach to attach cargo without immediate fruit removal) conflicts with designer's emphasis on clear wave progression and visible next fruit highlighting, potentially confusing players if fruit state updates lag visuals.

Implementation risks include: precise swept-segment collision detection complexity for probes vs. fruits and ship, correctly maintaining fixed-timestep integration without velocity sign-flips, and consistent state synchronization between probe cargo, hull, and probe stock across subsystems.
Missing tests include cross-subsystem integration tests validating combined visual, physics, collision, cargo banking, and HUD updates working together without regressions or visual glitches.

Mobile accessibility needs explicit verification: ensuring touch input responsiveness with the new zones, preventing frame drops due to orbital orbit rendering, and confirming no overflow or scroll occurs in targeted viewport sizes.

assessments.risk: Visual confusion if fruit wave rendering lags or conflicts with cargo state changes from probe pickups; also risk layout overflow in varied mobile viewports.
assessments.mitigation: Add integration tests with updated fruit state and probe cargo; verify UI zones resize and render correctly on 360x800 and similar screens; synchronize fruit state changes with cargo pickup events.

assessments.risk: Complex physics calculations for softened gravity and stable orbits may introduce non-determinism or performance issues, risking probe behavior stability.
assessments.mitigation: Implement thorough deterministic fixed-timestep physics tests; profile performance on target devices; modularize physics for clarity and debugging; collaborate with engineer on collision consistency.

assessments.risk: Collision handling with invulnerability cooldown, cargo banking logic, and HUD updating may cause inconsistent state or feedback if event timing conflicts or state updates are delayed.
assessments.mitigation: Implement precise event ordering with state locks; add unit tests for collision, cargo banking, and invulnerability logic; ensure HUD updates reflect latest game state without lag.

proposed_action.rationale: All three proposals address distinct yet interdependent subsystems: designer focuses on clear visual zones and fruit presentation, researcher advances realistic orbit and cargo mechanics, engineer handles collision physics and resource updates. Their careful integration can realize the cohesive gameplay envisioned, provided code conflicts are managed and tests cover integration points thoroughly.

required_evidence: Integration test results verifying combined 'gravitySlingSubsystem' behavior under fixed timestep without velocity sign flips.
Automated test logs showing correct fruit pickup order visuals synchronizing with cargo state changes across subsystems.
Performance benchmarks on representative mobile devices demonstrating stable frame rate with layered rendering and orbital probe visualization.
Collision subsystem unit and integration tests confirming hull damage, probe loss, and invulnerability cooldown correctness.
Mobile accessibility test reports for viewport sizes 360x800, 390x844, and 412x915 confirming layout stability and touch control responsiveness.

producer.claim: Integrate the designer, researcher, and engineer subsystems to fully implement the Peach Bounce 0.3 gameplay redesign.
producer.rationale: The designer subsystem provides a visually rich and clear fruit wave progression with the distinct top field and bottom ship control zones, essential for player spatial understanding in the portrait layout. The researcher subsystem offers stable, softened gravity orbital probe flight and nuanced cargo banking mechanics introducing meaningful skill and resource management. The engineer subsystem ensures accurate collision handling, cargo banking implementation, invulnerability cooldowns, and visual feedback to maintain consistent game state and survivable player progression. Combining these three yields a coherent gameplay experience fulfilling all user mechanics requirements without substituting any concept.
objections: Potential performance risks arise from the complex physics and collision code integration, which may affect deterministic behavior on devices.
The visual rendering by the designer may lag or conflict with cargo state changes from probe pickups, potentially causing player confusion.
Collision and invulnerability timing intricacies might lead to inconsistent state updates or delayed HUD feedback if not carefully ordered.

proposed_action.decision_reason: All three subsystems target crucial, complementary gameplay aspects—visual fruit presentation and layout, orbital probe physics with cargo banking, and collision plus resource state management—ensuring the player's full requested mechanics (ship horizontal movement, gravitational probe, sling/catch zone, hull/probe loss, depth fruit, ordered slowing waves) are implemented as per the binding work order without substituting core concepts. Their combined integration aligns precisely with 0.3 redesign requirements.
interface_contracts: GravitySlingSubsystem.position, velocity state shared between researcher and engineer modules
FruitWaveState with fruit order indices and visual state managed by designer and polled by researcher for collision detection
CargoCarriedByProbe array state manipulated by researcher and engineer subsystems
Ship.HorizontalPosition accessible for probe gravitational calculations and input handling across all subsystems
CollisionRadiusInner and CargoDepositAnnulusOuter radii constants shared by researcher and engineer
HUDState updated by engineer to reflect hull and probe stock changes influenced by cargo banking logic
integration_steps: Merge designer's renderFruitWaveAndPerspective into main game.js render loop ensuring layering matches cargo pickup state from researcher
Integrate researcher gravitySlingSubsystem with engineer's probeCollisionAndBanking, harmonizing position and velocity update calls to avoid duplicated physics integration
Combine engineer's shipCollisions and cargoBanking logic with researcher fruitPickupDetection to ensure correct event sequencing: collision, cargo attach, cargo bank
Coordinate interface contract constants defining ship collision and deposit radius in a shared physics config file included by researcher and engineer

Update main game step() to call unified input handling (designer ship horizontal drag), gravity probe physics (researcher), collision detection and resource updates (engineer) in correct deterministic fixed timestep order
Link designer's fruit wave UI highlighting to researcher engine fruitPickupDetection events for consistent NEXT target highlighting
verification: Playtest on portrait viewport 360x800 verifying fruit wave rendering matches assigned perspective scaling and NEXT fruit highlight
Run deterministic fixed timestep simulation to confirm near-miss probe orbit with simulated ship horizontal moves deposits cargo correctly outside collision radius
Trigger direct probe-ship collision verifying exactly 1 hull and 1 probe loss, damage feedback, and probe redeploy if probes remain
Force probe offscreen escape verifying 1 probe loss without hull damage and correct HUD updates
Test fruit collision order: hitting wrong fruit shows visual feedback but no cargo attach or resource gain
Confirm lost probe cargo cause fruit requeue without duplication or soft-lock
Verify touch and keyboard input move ship horizontally only in bottom zone, no UI layout overlap or scrolling
Pause, resume, and restart functions retain game state consistently across physics, UI, and resources

required_evidence: Deterministic fixed-step simulations demonstrating near-miss probe orbits and banking passes under integrated physics and collision code
Replay playtests on 360x800, 390x844, and 412x915 device emulations verifying stable frame rate and responsive input with combined subsystems active
Unit and integration tests confirming collision handling triggers appropriate hull/probe adjustments, invulnerability cooldown, and cargo banking logic in proper event order
Visual validation of fruit wave progression with next target highlight matching fruit pickup state after probe contact
HUD updates verifying correct sequential hull repair and probe increment resource accounting after banking
Source code reviews confirming interface contracts usage and synchronization between designer, researcher, and engineer modules
QA documented probe loss and cargo recovery tests ensuring no duplication or stuck waves
UI layout testing showing no vertical overflow, fixed instructions text, and stable input zones with safe-area paddings across viewport variants

coder_report:
# Peach Bounce 0.3 — implementation report

Implemented the binding complete redesign at the existing `docs/games/studio-original-001/` URL. Selected candidate IDs: **designer, researcher, engineer**, all integrated. Changed only the target's `index.html`, `game.css`, `game.js`, plus this report. The previous catch/tray/tile mechanics are removed; 0.2 remains recoverable in existing Git history. No metadata, publishing code, dependencies, other games, or tests were edited.

**Release status: implementation ready for runner verification; NOT approved for publication.** The independent browser gate could not launch Chrome in this restricted environment. No live deployment, live-byte comparison, physical-phone verification, independent QA approval, footage inspection, or real browser playtest is claimed.

## Integrated source changes

| Selected candidate | Concrete implementation | Verification and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| designer | `index.html`: persistent Peach Bounce/version 0.3, compact HUD, concise instructions, host control IDs, initial LOCAL BUILD label. `game.css`: safe-area padding, flex canvas, 44px controls, compact header. `draw`/`fruit` in JS: shaded upper 60% field, lower ship zone, perspective grid, depth-sized peach/pear/plum shapes, numbered targets, NEXT ring, depth-sorted drawing. `wave`/`step`: continuing ordered waves, increasingly offset targets, gradual slowing downward fruit movement constrained to upper field. | Model checks confirm ordered state/progression. Synthetic rendering and callback checks completed at dimensions representing all three requested phones and desktop; these do not prove actual CSS bounds, screenshots, frame rate, or physical-device readability. |
| researcher | One pure `createGame` fixed-step model replaces the old crossing/catch flip. `initial` sets an upward tangential launch; `acceleration` computes softened inverse-square ship gravity; `integrate` performs continuous semi-implicit integration. `step` applies swept relative ship collision, then escape, ordered swept fruit contact, then near-pass banking. Probe trail, dashed gravity tether, visible carried fruit, collision and deposit rings render from actual model state. | Ten deterministic checks pass, including a natural complete orbit with pickups and banking. At model height 575: banking at 9.075 game seconds, minimum center distance 51.998 units, maximum velocity change in one 1/120-second step 13.005 units/second; no instantaneous catch flip or teleport. |
| engineer | `lose`: exactly one loss per active flight; crash costs one hull and one probe, escape costs only one probe; cargo targets requeue. Inactive probe guard prevents duplicate charges. Replacement delay 0.9 seconds exceeds the 0.8-second damage cooldown; one automatic deployment per lost flight. `bank`: FIFO units repair hull first, then build probes to capacity; each target has available/carried/banked state. Banking requires armed approach followed by outward deposit boundary crossing. Age/offscreen/distance limits prevent stuck flights. Hull/probe exhaustion ends the run; Play/Restart resets it. | Direct crash, escape, damage feedback state, single redeployment, wrong-order rejection, safe deposit, collision precedence, unit priority, full stores, no repeated credit, cargo recovery, defeat/replay and timeout checks pass. Real browser feedback and controls await runner QA. |

## Shared interface contracts and integration

- Gravity position/velocity: the single `state.probe` (`x`, `y`, `vx`, `vy`) is integrated once per tick and consumed by collision, pickup, deposit, rendering, and diagnostics.
- Fruit wave state: `state.fruits`, numeric `id`, and `status` (`available`, `carried`, `banked`) are authoritative for both NEXT and contact eligibility. Carried fruit leaves the field drawing immediately but remains in wave accounting until banked; on loss it returns to available. Banked fruit cannot pay twice or requeue.
- Cargo: `state.probe.cargo` holds ordered fruit IDs. Banking drains it FIFO; loss clears it after restoring only carried IDs. New waves begin only when every current target is banked.
- Horizontal ship state: `state.player.x` is driven by a bounded fixed-step input, while `y` stays in the bottom zone. Pointer coordinates are inverted through the same uniform transform used for drawing. Keyboard A/D and left/right arrows drive the same input. W/S/up/down are handled without moving the ship vertically.
- Shared geometry: frozen `PHYSICS` is the one constants source used for simulation, rendering and snapshot. Hull radius 20 plus probe collision radius 5; safe deposit annulus 32–76; softening 18; gravity parameter 5,000,000. No separate JSON/config fetch was necessary. Sharing these constants inline instead of introducing a proposed config file avoids extra load/state coordination.
- HUD state: all resource values, messages and cargo counts come from the model, without parallel resource bookkeeping. Probe stock includes the active probe: launch does not charge stock; destruction/escape does. Maximum hull is 3, maximum stock 8. Each banked fruit also increments the visible banked score by one, including when stores are full, but cannot exceed resource caps.
- Integration order: ship input → moving fruit → single gravity integration → swept solid collision → flight loss → ordered pickup → qualified outward deposit → wave advancement. A collision aborts that tick before rewards. A fresh launch inside the deposit radius is not an armed return.

## Request criteria

1. **Identity/scope:** title, persistent `game-version` 0.3, stable directory, local script/styles, no services/assets/dependencies. `build-version` is initially LOCAL BUILD and JS never writes it. Runner must stamp the distinct release build before its gate/publication.
2. **Portrait layout:** viewport-height flex structure allocates remaining room to canvas, retains all controls, includes safe-area padding and a compact instruction/status region. Uniform rendering uses letterboxing after aspect changes rather than independently stretching axes. Actual no-scroll/overlap/tappable-bounds verification on 360×800, 390×844, 412×915 remains unverified because browser execution was blocked.
3. **Orbital motion:** 120 Hz physics with bounded accumulated real-frame time, softened gravity, initial tangential momentum, continuous velocity updates and bounded maximum speed. Ship movement changes the actual gravity center; no return crossing sets `vy` or teleports the probe.
4. **Loss accounting:** swept ship collision consumes exactly one hull and stock; offscreen, excess distance or flight age over 24 seconds consumes stock only. One replacement after 0.9 seconds if alive; clean defeat otherwise.
5. **Ordered pickup:** swept segment contact attaches only the first available numbered fruit. Wrong-order fruit flashes and remains. Contact does not repair/build/score. Cargo icons follow the probe.
6. **Banking:** a flight must first leave the outer ring, approach through its safe annulus, and cross outward again. Solid collision has priority. Cargo is consumed exactly once at deposit.
7. **Economy:** each unit repairs one missing hull before any stock is built; full stores remain capped. Messages distinguish repairs, builds, full stores, crash and escape.
8. **Recovery:** lost carried targets become available again with unchanged identities. Already banked targets remain banked. NEXT is derived from the first available target, preventing ordered-wave lock or duplicate profit.
9. **Progression/end state:** indefinite survival waves replace the three-wave win demo. Three to six targets per wave, increasing lateral offsets/drift, replenishment via banking. Initial waves teach a viable path; idle play eventually loses on later waves. Defeat is clear and replayable. No separate victory is claimed for this survival design.
10. **Controls/state:** host IDs preserved. Play starts; Pause remains enabled to Resume and freezes all simulation time; Restart starts clean. Pointer release/cancel/lost capture clears input; keyboard and blur/visibility pausing remain. Read-only frozen BORHEZ_GAME API returns newly copied actual state, including nested probe/cargo/fruit/event data. Reduced motion suppresses the trail and decorative movement; necessary physics/fruit movement remains.
11. **Evidence/publication:** deterministic and synthetic tests below passed. Independent real browser/mobile input, screenshot, performance, stamped-build and live-byte checks remain runner responsibilities. Do not publish based solely on this report.

## Commands actually run and results

- Read `artifacts/mobile/job.json`, `plan.json`, `feedback.md`, the existing three source files, and the shared acceptance script. No prior `gate.log` was present to repair.
- `node --check docs/games/studio-original-001/game.js` — PASS, including after the final edit.
- `node /tmp/peach-physics.cjs` — PASS, 10 deterministic assertions against the same CommonJS-exported model used in browser gameplay. Final run output: all ten checks passed. Test source is reproduced below so the temporary harness is not required for reproduction.
- `node /tmp/peach-dom.cjs` — PASS at synthetic viewport inputs 360×800, 390×844, 412×915 and 1280×800. Node VM with mock DOM/canvas invoked actual registered application callbacks and frame loop: Play advances, drag moves x by 90 model units while y remains fixed, cancel releases, pause freezes, Resume advances, Restart resets, A key moves ship, build label is unchanged, API is frozen. The mock geometry was assigned (canvas widths 344/374/396/480 and heights 589/633/704/589), not measured by a layout engine. **These are not real pointer events/browser tests and are not independent QA.**
- Additional inline Node simulations: at heights 340/530/575/650/720, idle runs progressed through three waves then lost at wave 4, with nine banked fruit and no hull damage, after 121.558/98.758/107.092/122.175/137.342 simulated seconds respectively. This confirms a complete finite loss loop for idle play rather than a permanently stuck orbit.
- Additional inline Node input replay: for heights 530/575/650, run 1900 fixed ticks; right input on ticks 120–125, left on 126–131, otherwise zero. All three produced three banked fruit, hull 3 and stock 7 at 15.833 simulated seconds. This is a reproducible steering-and-banking model path, not a browser/phone playtest.
- `curl ... http://127.0.0.1:8765/games/studio-original-001/` — unavailable (curl exit 7, HTTP 000).
- `python -m http.server 8765 --directory docs` — FAILED before serving: `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` creating a socket. No server was started.
- `node game_factory/mobile_acceptance.cjs` — BLOCKED/FAILED before loading the game: Chrome process terminated with SIGTRAP; Crashpad `setsockopt: Operation not permitted (1)`. No acceptance pass is claimed. The runner must rerun in an environment that permits supplied browser/server operation. Tests were not weakened or edited.
- `git diff --check` — PASS. Working-tree review showed only the three authorized target source changes (the report is in the ignored artifacts directory).

## Remaining limitations

Real browser mobile/desktop input, actual CSS layout, rendered visual clarity, frame rate, low-end/physical device behavior, screenshots and independent gameplay QA could not be verified. Rotation preserves collision geometry via uniform letterboxing; it does not regenerate the current flight to fill a new aspect ratio. Difficulty and advanced steering balance need browser QA beyond the demonstrated first-wave survival path. Natural gravity precession can send later passes offscreen; that is handled as an escape and replacements remain earnable. Initial teaching waves intentionally allow a centered no-input bank; later offsets require trajectory intervention. No claim of indefinitely sustainable expert play is made.

## Reproducible deterministic harness

Run from repository root using Node; the CommonJS branch exports the actual model without creating a DOM or exposing browser write access. Scenario state injection is confined to this Node harness for specific collision/accounting cases; the natural orbit and input replays do not inject probe progress.

const assert=require('node:assert/strict');const {createGame,DT}=require(process.cwd()+'/docs/games/studio-original-001/game.js');let passed=0;function test(name,fn){fn();console.log('PASS',name);passed++;}function fresh(){const g=createGame(575);g.reset();return g;}function ticks(g,n){for(let i=0;i<n;i++)g.step();}function carry(g,ids){for(const id of ids)g.state.fruits.find(f=>f.id===id).status='carried';g.state.probe.cargo=ids.slice();}function outgoing(g){Object.assign(g.state.probe,{x:g.state.player.x+75,y:g.state.player.y,vx:300,vy:0,near:true,armed:true});g.step();}
test('natural continuous near-miss orbit, ordered pickups, bank, continuing waves',()=>{const g=fresh();let maxDelta=0,old={...g.state.probe};for(let i=0;i<1200&&!g.state.bankings;i++){g.step();const p=g.state.probe;maxDelta=Math.max(maxDelta,Math.hypot(p.vx-old.vx,p.vy-old.vy));old={...p};}assert.equal(g.state.score,3);assert.equal(g.state.probes,8);assert.equal(g.state.wave,2);assert.equal(g.state.crashes,0);assert.ok(g.state.probe.minDistance>32);assert.ok(maxDelta<20);console.log({bankTime:g.state.time,minDistance:g.state.probe.minDistance,maxVelocityStep:maxDelta});});
test('direct collision exactly -1 hull -1 probe; no duplicate loss; replacement once',()=>{const g=fresh();Object.assign(g.state.probe,{x:180,y:g.state.player.y-26,vx:0,vy:300});g.step();assert.equal(g.state.hull,2);assert.equal(g.state.probes,4);assert.ok(g.state.invulnerability>0);ticks(g,90);assert.equal(g.state.probes,4);assert.equal(g.state.flight,1);ticks(g,22);assert.equal(g.state.flight,2);assert.equal(g.state.crashes,1);});
test('escape only costs a probe; unbanked cargo requeues in order; no duplicate money',()=>{const g=fresh();carry(g,[1,2]);Object.assign(g.state.probe,{x:361,y:100,vx:50,vy:0});g.step();assert.equal(g.state.hull,3);assert.equal(g.state.probes,4);assert.equal(g.state.score,0);assert.equal(g.snapshot().next,1);assert.ok(g.state.fruits.every(f=>f.status==='available'));assert.equal(g.state.probe.cargo.length,0);ticks(g,20);assert.equal(g.state.probes,4);});
test('wrong-order swept contact stays available and adds no cargo or money',()=>{const g=fresh();const f=g.state.fruits[1];Object.assign(g.state.probe,{x:f.x-22,y:f.y,vx:650,vy:0});ticks(g,4);assert.equal(f.status,'available');assert.equal(g.state.probe.cargo.length,0);assert.equal(g.state.score,0);assert.ok(g.state.events.some(e=>e.type==='wrong'));});
test('repair before construction, each unit once; capacities; lingering cannot bank twice',()=>{const g=fresh();g.state.hull=1;g.state.probes=7;carry(g,[1,2,3]);outgoing(g);assert.equal(g.state.hull,3);assert.equal(g.state.probes,8);assert.equal(g.state.score,3);outgoing(g);assert.equal(g.state.score,3);carry(g,[1,2,3]);outgoing(g);assert.equal(g.state.probes,8);assert.equal(g.state.score,6);});
test('solid radius always crashes instead of banking',()=>{const g=fresh();g.state.hull=2;carry(g,[1]);Object.assign(g.state.probe,{x:180,y:g.state.player.y-26,vx:0,vy:300,near:true});g.step();assert.equal(g.state.hull,1);assert.equal(g.state.probes,4);assert.equal(g.state.score,0);assert.equal(g.snapshot().next,1);});
test('ring requires approach then departure; mere fruit pickup gives no repair',()=>{const g=fresh();g.state.hull=2;carry(g,[1]);Object.assign(g.state.probe,{x:180+60,y:g.state.player.y,vx:0,vy:-100,armed:false});g.step();assert.equal(g.state.score,0);assert.equal(g.state.hull,2);});
test('paused time/state freezes; resume advances; reset is clean; snapshots independent',()=>{const g=fresh();ticks(g,100);g.state.mode='paused';const a=g.snapshot();ticks(g,100);assert.deepEqual(g.snapshot(),a);g.state.mode='running';g.step();assert.ok(g.state.time>a.time);a.player.x=1;assert.notEqual(g.state.player.x,1);g.reset();assert.equal(g.state.time,0);assert.equal(g.state.score,0);assert.equal(g.state.flight,1);assert.equal(g.state.probe.cargo.length,0);});

test('player motion changes actual flight; deterministic repeat',()=>{function run(input){const g=fresh();for(let i=0;i<360;i++)g.step(DT,i>240?input:0);return g.snapshot();}assert.deepEqual(run(.1),run(.1));assert.notEqual(run(.1).probe.x,run(0).probe.x);});
